key_insight: Token-level statistical typicality against an expert model provides a trust signal that complements a generative model’s own confidence.
engineering_relevance: Combining expert-reference scores with conventional uncertainty statistics can support detectors of unreliable generated code, mathematical solutions, and medical answers.
method: Use an expert model’s token distribution as a reference, not as factual ground truth.
Train an AI ontology calibrator using student-model latent features and token-level statistics to estimate expert-reference acceptance scores.
Aggregate calibrator scores, confidence, entropy, and perplexity into 15 response-level indicators for correctness classification.
evidence_signal: Evaluations on BF program generation, mathematical problem solving, and medical question answering found complementary reliability signals and cross-domain detector transfer, though transfer was not always symmetric.
watch_item: Expert-reference typicality does not establish factual correctness, and transfer reliability may depend on the source and target domains.
paper_title: A statistical measure of trust in generative AI
